thread:
Aisha (Product PM): ACME asked if we can deliver a sprint-slot allocator that prefetches tenant model weights + KV prefixes to reduce cold-starts. They want a deterministic Q3 ship. Need cross-team alignment: runtime, infra, security.
Dan (Eng): quick clarifying q: is this global prewarm or per-tenant opt-in?
Aisha (Product PM): per-tenant opt-in to start. Product flips a tenant flag for pilot customers. Goals: reduce cold-start p95 for target tenants, keep p95 for others unchanged, and limit cost bump to <=8%.
Priya (Runtime): runtime concerns: 1) memory + KV eviction pressure when many tenants are "warmed"; 2) prefetch scheduling mustn't interfere with steady-state batching.
Priya (Runtime): proposed design: tenant-level prefetch queue that runs during configured off-peak windows. When a prefetch completes, mark tenant "warmed" with TTL. If warm flag absent, fall back to cold start.
Priya (Runtime): example config we can use for rollout: {"prefetch": {"enabled": true, "window": "02:00-05:00 UTC", "warm_ttl_hours": "6", "max_concurrent_prefetch": "8"}}
Jorge (Infra): infra needs estimates for reserved GPU minutes, peak prefetch concurrency, and whether warmed artifacts need additional ephemeral storage. If we need new SKUs there's a 48h provisioning lead. I'll open a capacity ticket.
Dan (Eng): runtime should emit these metrics: prefetch_tasks_pending, prefetch_success_rate, warmed_tenants_count, prefetch_gpu_mins. Also tracing tags to tie requests to warm vs cold path.
Priya (Runtime): will add those metrics. We'll keep cardinality low (bucket by customer class) to avoid metrics cost.
Lena (Security): if prefetch touches encrypted model checkpoints or KMS, we need audit trails. Confirmed prefetch is ephemeral memory-only?
Aisha (Product PM): yes, ephemeral caches only. Product requires an opt-in audit event and asserts prefetch must not pull any tenant PII.
Lena (Security): ok. Security acceptance: 1) opt-in/out audit events; 2) code review focused on secret access; 3) rate-limited KMS calls if used.
Dan (Eng): proposed timeline if Q3 ship: spike + prototype 2 weeks, internal canary week 3, 2-week canary validation, customer pilot week 6. Tight but workable for MVP.
Jorge (Infra): note on autoscaler: if burst nodes are needed, we must schedule capacity changes ahead (48h). If we can fit inside existing pools with node-level throttles we avoid the lead.
Priya (Runtime): runtime acceptance criteria: a) warm path reduces cold-start p95 by >=40% for test tenants; b) warm path adds <5% CPU/GPU overhead during peak; c) feature-flag rollback drains prefetch queue and clears warm flags.
Aisha (Product PM): combined launch criteria: - p95 tail for pilot tenants improved per goal - total cost delta <= 8% - security checklist green - canary stable for 2 weeks with no incidents and alert thresholds respected.
Dan (Eng): test plan: replay tenant traces, run e2e warm/unwarm cycles, validate metrics and alerting. Add canary alerts: prefetch_fail_rate > 1% or warmed_tenant_errors increase => rollback.
Lena (Security): scheduling a 1-hour review window tomorrow. Need opt-in event spec and a pointer to the PR.
Priya (Runtime): I'll post a PR tomorrow with queue + metrics + feature flag and a draft rollout config.
OpsBot: deploy-bot scheduled job deploy/canary-prefetch 2026-04-06T03:00:00Z and will notify #eng-oncall.
Aisha (Product PM): ask: please reply with "ack" + time estimate (hours) by EOD so I can lock into the roadmap.
Dan (Eng): ack 40h (includes tests).
Priya (Runtime): ack 56h (queue, metrics, rollout config, tests).
Jorge (Infra): ack 24h (capacity ticket + autoscaler tuning), note +48h if new SKUs needed.
Lena (Security): ack 8h (review + follow-ups).
Aisha (Product PM): great. I'll draft the formal spec and add to the Q3 slate. :rocket:
